summary: When a courtroom is closed, a defendant may be entitled to admit a nonfamily supporter with a significant relationship (like a counselor) absent a specific safety basis for exclusion. Excluding defendant's drug counselor without inquiry violated the public-trial right; conviction reversed and new trial ordered.

CPL 440.30 (1-a) imposes no due-diligence time limit for postconviction DNA motions, and defendants need not prove evidence availability because that burden is on the People. Pitts's denial was affirmed on lack of likely different verdict, while Barnwell's case was reversed and remitted for further proceedings.

The CPL permits filing a new information that adds facts and charges additional offenses from the same criminal transaction before plea or trial. Reinstatement of the superseding/successive informations was affirmed.
Admission of a nontestifying codefendant's plea allocution violated Crawford and was not harmless beyond a reasonable doubt. Conviction reversed and new trial ordered.
Admission of a codefendant plea allocution was Crawford error, but harmless beyond a reasonable doubt given strong independent proof. Conviction affirmed.
County Court properly denied withdrawal of a negotiated felony-murder plea where the allocution did not negate guilt or voluntariness. Conviction affirmed.
Defendant satisfied the Shield Law test for nonconfidential media outtakes of his police interrogation, and quashing the subpoena was error. Conviction reversed and new trial ordered.
A denial of a CPL 210.30 grand-jury sufficiency motion is not reviewable after conviction supported by legally sufficient trial evidence. Order affirming conviction was sustained.
Mandatory postrelease supervision is a direct consequence of a determinate sentence; failure to advise defendant before a guilty plea requires vacatur. Plea was reversed and case remitted.

Counsel's disclosure of an ethical dilemma and use of narrative testimony did not deny effective assistance, and defendant had no right to be present for the attorney-court colloquy. Conviction affirmed.

Reliance on an untranslated diary without court review was error. Case was modified and remitted for in camera inspection, with new trial only if undisclosed material creates a reasonable possibility of affecting the verdict under CPL 240.75.
The castle exception to retreat did not apply where defendant stood in an apartment doorway opening to a common hall; retreat instruction was proper. Conviction affirmed.
An order of protection with a 100-year expiration date was a permissible way to effectuate a maximum-duration protective order for a life sentence. Conviction and order were affirmed.
Vehicle and Traffic Law authority allowed a fire chief to delegate traffic-control duties at fire/accident scenes to subordinate firefighters. Conviction/order affirmed.

The People cannot directly appeal under CPL 450.20 from a trial court's sua sponte verdict set-aside under Judiciary Law 2-b; the proper vehicle is CPLR article 78. Dismissal of the People's appeal was affirmed.

A nonparty has no right to intervene in a criminal appeal under the CPL; participation is by amicus application, not intervention. Hybrid Films' intervention motion was denied and reargument dismissed.

Excluding third-party culpability proof (photo/evidence about another robber) was within the trial court's Primo balancing discretion where no sufficient nexus to this robbery was shown. Evidence was legally sufficient and ineffective-assistance claims failed; conviction affirmed.
NYC DEP Water Supply Police have statutory authority to enforce traffic laws in the watershed. Dismissed traffic informations were reinstated and lower orders reversed.
Peace officers acting under color of office outside their jurisdiction cannot justify a stop as a private citizen's arrest. Suppression/dismissal rulings were affirmed.
Trial court did not abuse discretion by precluding an untimely psychiatric exam for an insanity defense where notice came at jury selection after tactical delay. Conviction affirmed.

A criminal-trespass information was facially defective for failing to allege the Penal Law 140.10 (a) element that the building/property was fenced or otherwise enclosed to exclude intruders. Dismissal was affirmed.

Consecutive sentencing for weapon possession and the homicide/assault counts violated Penal Law 70.25 (2) where the same gun-use conduct overlapped materially. Order modified to vacate weapon sentence and remit for resentencing.
Post-Apprendi Supreme Court cases did not undermine People v Rosen; New York's persistent felony offender scheme remained constitutional as applied. Sentence and order affirmed.

A jury instruction telling jurors not to speculate about uncalled witnesses improperly undercut defendant's core argument about lack of corroboration in a one-witness buy-and-bust case. Reversal by the Appellate Division was affirmed.
Persistent felony offender Apprendi challenge failed under Rivera; the Court declined to decide whether the issue could be raised for the first time in a CPL 440.20 motion. Order affirmed.
Coconspirator statements were properly admitted, accomplice-as-a-matter-of-law and ineffective-assistance claims failed, and corroboration was sufficient. Conspiracy conviction was affirmed.
The Treaty of Canandaigua did not preserve Tuscarora off-reservation fishing rights on former Seneca lands after the Seneca conveyance. Conviction for violating fishing-tag regulation was affirmed.
Unpreserved Apprendi attacks on persistent felony offender sentences failed on the merits under Rivera even assuming mode-of-proceedings treatment. Both affirmances were upheld.

After dismissal of a defective indictment, plea by superior court information on identical terms was permissible where re-presentation was contemplated and defendant knowingly waived indictment. Conviction affirmed.
Defendant was entitled to present reputation-for-truthfulness impeachment of key prosecution witnesses; exclusion of that evidence was reversible error. Order reversed and new trial ordered.

A court officer's unauthorized jury-room demonstration was not an unwaivable mode-of-proceedings defect where the judge resumed control, consulted counsel, and gave a curative instruction accepted by defendant. Conviction affirmed.

One unwarned handwritten statement was suppressible, but later Mirandized statements were admissible because they were not part of a single continuous chain of events under Chapple/Bethea; any error was harmless. Conviction affirmed.
Denial of Mapp/Dunaway hearing was proper where suppression allegations were conclusory and defendant's own disclosed statement established probable cause. Order affirmed.
CPL 180.50 inquiry was unnecessary where the felony count was dismissed rather than reduced and defendant pleaded guilty to separately charged misdemeanors. Order affirmed.
Any failure to conduct a CPL 180.50 reduction inquiry was forfeited by defendant's guilty plea. Order affirmed.

Grand-jury integrity was impaired where prosecutor gave misleading/noninformative answers about defense-requested alibi witnesses, potentially prejudicing defendant. Indictment dismissal with leave to re-present was affirmed.

Lineup was unduly suggestive after pre-lineup photo viewing; because independent source was never properly determined and record was inadequate for de novo review, conviction was reversed and remitted for an independent-source hearing before retrial.
Ineffective-assistance claim based on alleged uncommunicated/forgone plea failed because defendant did not substantiate that he would have accepted the offer. Order affirmed.
Consent obtained during an unsupported common-law inquiry lacked the required founded suspicion of criminality under Hollman. Suppression ruling and Appellate Division order were affirmed.

Death sentence was vacated under Hynes/Harris-era death-penalty precedent, but numerous trial and conviction challenges were rejected. Judgment modified to vacate death sentence and remit for resentencing; convictions otherwise affirmed.

General consent to search a car did not authorize a destructive search using a crowbar to pry open a hidden compartment/gas tank; scope of consent was exceeded. Order reversed and remitted for consideration of unresolved probable-cause issues.

Counsel was ineffective where both trial and appellate attorneys failed to raise a dispositive statute-of-limitations bar to manslaughter as a lesser count. Coram nobis relief vacating the conviction was properly granted and affirmed.

No claim-of-right jury instruction is available in robbery prosecutions, even for specific property allegedly owned by defendant; policy and statutory text confine the defense to specified larceny offenses. Conviction affirmed.

For burglary, intended crime can be conduct violating an order of protection inside the premises, but mere intent to enter in violation of the order cannot alone satisfy the 'intent to commit a crime therein' element. Conviction affirmed on preservation and sufficiency grounds.
New York had territorial jurisdiction over California drug-possession counts under CPL 20.20 (1) (c) based on conspiratorial conduct in New York to possess/transport cocaine. Convictions affirmed.
For school-zone drug-sale offenses, the 1,000-foot distance is measured by straight line, not pedestrian route. Conviction affirmed.

Per se reversal for representation by an imposter did not apply where an admitted attorney actively served as lead counsel throughout and no prejudice was shown from limited nonlawyer participation. Conviction affirmed.
Defendant was entitled to a lesser-included criminal-trespass charge where evidence permitted inference he lacked intent to burglarize at entry. Conviction reversed and new trial ordered.
People's appeal was dismissed as moot after County Court resentenced defendant to the same term as before.
Defendant failed to rebut the presumption of regularity regarding sidebar juror questioning after being advised of the right to be present. Order affirmed.
Psychiatric expert basis testimony repeating testimonial statements from non-testifying interviewees violated Crawford and was not harmless. Conviction reversed and new trial ordered.
Juror-misconduct and Buford inquiry claims were unpreserved or unsupported, and alleged new evidence was equivocal impeachment material insufficient under CPL 330.30. Conviction affirmed.
Limiting cross-examination into specific circumstances of a witness's delayed accusation did not violate confrontation rights or constitute abuse of discretion on this record. Conviction affirmed.

One-on-one fatal stabbings in these cases did not fit depraved-indifference murder; depravity is distinct from intent and cannot be inferred merely from grave risk. Depraved-indifference convictions were reversed and remitted.

Defendant forfeited challenge to continued deliberations after a partial verdict where he endorsed the procedure and failed to object despite non-Boettcher submission. First-degree murder conviction affirmed.
